full_description: Web Design for Kids — HTML & CSS Foundations is an engaging, age-appropriate, project-based 6-week (32 learning hours) certification program for children aged 10–16. Students learn to build authentic web pages using genuine HTML5 and CSS, mastering document structure, typography, color palettes, spacing, the CSS box model, Flexbox layouts, mobile responsiveness, semantic tags, image alternative text, and browser developer tools. The course culminates in an original personal-interest website portfolio presented through a local browser demonstration or optional parent-approved static showcase, adhering strictly to child privacy and digital safety.

overview.description: Introduce young learners to creative website design with HTML and CSS. Learn page structure, typography, images, colours, layouts, responsiveness and internet safety while creating original web pages and a personal project showcase.
expandedCopy: Discover how websites are built by writing HTML to organize content and CSS to create visual designs. Students learn to add text, images, links and navigation before exploring layouts that adapt to different screen sizes.

Through guided coding challenges and an original website project, learners practise planning, building, testing and improving their own pages. They also learn simple accessibility principles and how to protect personal information online.

Genuine HTML5 and CSS coding — not drag-and-drop website builders

Creative styling: color harmony, readable typography, spacing, and CSS box model
Modern layout foundations: Flexbox rows/columns, flexible widths, and fluid cards
Responsive design: mobile viewport testing and adapting to screens without horizontal scroll

curriculum.title: How Websites Work
curriculum.objective: Understand the basic structure of websites and create simple interconnected HTML pages.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Create a simple HTML homepage featuring a heading, short introduction to a fictional or non-identifying topic, paragraphs, lists, one appropriate image, and at least one working link.
curriculum.practical_assignment: Create a basic homepage and a second linked HTML page with working relative navigation.
curriculum.assessment: Explain HTML purpose, create a valid basic document, add structured content, link pages, and open the result locally in a web browser.

curriculum.title: Creative CSS & Visual Design
curriculum.objective: Style webpages using CSS while learning typography, colour, spacing and basic visual design principles.

lessons.title: Adding CSS
topics: Basic inline styles for explanation only
Why external CSS helps maintain consistency

lessons.title: The Cascade
topics: Why a style may not apply

lessons.title: Readable Text
topics: Avoiding decorative fonts for long paragraphs

curriculum.hands_on_lab: Style a basic HTML website using an original colour scheme, readable font choices, consistent spacing, styled headings, and cards or content sections.
curriculum.practical_assignment: Create a consistent stylesheet for the homepage and hobby/project page.
curriculum.assessment: Check correct CSS link, basic selectors, colour choices, typography, box model application, visual consistency, and readability.

curriculum.title: Layouts & Responsive Design
curriculum.objective: Organize website content into simple layouts that remain usable across mobile, tablet and desktop screens.

lessons.title: Mobile-First Thinking
topics: Start with a simple stacked layout

lessons.title: Responsive Navigation Without JavaScript
topics: Simple wrapping or vertically stacked navigation

curriculum.hands_on_lab: Build a responsive navigation area, at least one Flexbox layout, a card or image gallery, and a layout that adapts seamlessly at narrow screen widths.
curriculum.practical_assignment: Make the current website draft usable across both mobile and desktop widths without horizontal scrolling.
curriculum.assessment: Verify zero significant horizontal overflow, readable typography, functional navigation, responsive fluid images, correct Flexbox usage, and appropriate mobile adaptation.

curriculum.title: Accessibility & Web Quality
curriculum.objective: Improve website usability through semantic HTML, image accessibility, readable content, keyboard access and basic debugging.

lessons.title: Heading Structure
topics: Avoiding headings used only for styling

lessons.title: Meaningful Alt Text
topics: Use empty alt text for genuinely decorative images

lessons.title: Accessible Typography
topics: Avoiding text embedded only inside images

lessons.title: Colour Independence
topics: Do not communicate essential meaning using colour alone

curriculum.hands_on_lab: Review a deliberately imperfect sample webpage with missing alt text, poor contrast, broken link, incorrect heading order, and narrow-screen overflow. Identify and fix the issues.
curriculum.practical_assignment: Prepare a basic accessibility checklist, navigation test, image alt-text review, colour contrast review, responsive test, and debugging notes.
curriculum.assessment: Evaluate actual webpage improvements in semantic structure, image alt attributes, contrast readability, keyboard focus, and mobile usability.

curriculum.title: Original Website Capstone
curriculum.objective: Complete and demonstrate an original, mobile-responsive website using student-written HTML and CSS.

lessons.title: Improvement
topics: Fix one or more identified issues

curriculum.hands_on_lab: Complete and test the final website across desktop and simulated mobile viewports, confirming keyboard access, link integrity, and styling consistency.
curriculum.practical_assignment: Submit original personal-interest website source files, completed testing checklist, and present a private showcase to instructor or parents.
curriculum.expected_deliverable: Complete HTML/CSS Website + Source Files + Testing Checklist + Private Showcase
curriculum.assessment: Evaluate HTML document structure, CSS styling, responsive layout, accessibility best practices, originality, child safety compliance, and student explanation.

faq.question: What is Web Design for Kids — HTML & CSS Foundations?
faq.answer: It is a beginner course where children learn to create and style webpages using HTML and CSS.

faq.question: What age group is recommended?
faq.answer: The course is recommended for ages 10–16.

faq.question: How long is the course?
faq.answer: Six weeks with 32 learning hours.

faq.question: What is the course fee?
faq.answer: ₹4,900, subject to verified Nova Skills pricing and tax policy.

faq.question: Is coding experience required?
faq.answer: No. The course starts with website and HTML fundamentals.

faq.question: What is HTML?
faq.answer: HTML defines the structure and meaning of a webpage's content.

faq.question: What is CSS?
faq.answer: CSS controls the visual appearance and layout of webpages.

faq.question: Will my child build a real website?
faq.answer: Yes. Students create a working multipage HTML/CSS website.

faq.question: Will the website work on mobile screens?
faq.answer: Students learn foundational responsive design and test their site at different screen sizes.

faq.question: What pages will the project include?
faq.answer: A homepage, hobby/project page and an original gallery or information section.

faq.question: Will students learn navigation?
faq.answer: Yes. They will create working links between pages.

faq.question: Will students learn Flexbox?
faq.answer: Yes. Flexbox is introduced for beginner layouts and responsive content.

faq.question: Will students learn basic design principles?
faq.answer: Yes. The course covers typography, colour, spacing, alignment and visual hierarchy.

faq.question: Will students use Canva?
faq.answer: Canva may support optional visual assets where age-appropriate and approved. It is not mandatory.

faq.question: What software is needed?
faq.answer: A suitable local code editor and modern browser.

faq.question: Is Glitch required?
faq.answer: No. Glitch project hosting ended in July 2025. The course uses local HTML/CSS tools instead.

faq.question: Must my child publish the website online?
faq.answer: No. A local website and private demonstration are valid.

faq.question: Does my child need a domain name?
faq.answer: No. A custom domain is not required.

faq.question: Does my child need a hosting account?
faq.answer: No. Online publishing is optional and must follow appropriate adult supervision and platform rules.

faq.question: Will students share their real names or photographs?
faq.answer: No. The course does not require identifiable personal information to be published.

faq.question: What is web accessibility?
faq.answer: Web accessibility means making websites easier for people with different needs to perceive, navigate and use.

faq.question: Will students learn image alt text?
faq.answer: Yes. Appropriate image descriptions are included in the curriculum.

faq.question: Will students learn keyboard navigation?
faq.answer: Yes. They will check basic link and focus behaviour using a keyboard.

faq.question: Will students learn to debug websites?
faq.answer: Yes. They will practise finding common HTML/CSS errors using browser tools and source inspection.

faq.question: Will the course teach JavaScript?
faq.answer: No. JavaScript applications are outside this foundational HTML/CSS course.

faq.question: Will the course teach e-commerce?
faq.answer: No. E-commerce systems and payment processing are separate advanced topics.

faq.question: Is this a professional web development qualification?
faq.answer: No. It is an introductory creative web design certification for young learners.

faq.question: Will parents see the finished website?
faq.answer: The portfolio includes a private parent-facing project showcase, subject to actual delivery arrangements.

faq.question: Is this different from using a website builder?
faq.answer: Yes. Students learn the underlying HTML and CSS rather than relying entirely on a template interface.

faq.question: What can children learn next?
faq.answer: Depending on readiness, they may progress to age-appropriate JavaScript foundations, Young Coders Program or other Kids Tech Academy courses.
